prompt: Why does enabling enable.idempotence=true and Kafka transactions NOT guarantee end-to-end exactly-once semantics when sinking to S3, PostgreSQL, or BigQuery, and how do you actually achieve it?
expected_tradeoffs: Kafka EOS only spans Kafka-to-Kafka read-process-write; external sinks require idempotent keys/deterministic upserts or 2PC/outbox, trading write amplification or latency for correctness.
anti_pattern_traps: claiming Kafka EOS alone gives end-to-end exactly-once across external sinks

prompt: Why do frequent CDC upserts using Apache Iceberg v2 equality deletes destroy Trino/Spark/DuckDB read latency even when total row count is small, and how do you remediate it?
expected_tradeoffs: Equality deletes avoid read-before-write on the writer (fast streaming ingest) but force every reader to evaluate delete predicates across data files until compaction converts/merges them.
anti_pattern_traps: recommending equality deletes without a compaction/rewrite_data_files cadence

prompt: When does Spark 3.x Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) silently fail to mitigate data skew or coalesce shuffle partitions?
expected_tradeoffs: AQE only re-optimizes at shuffle/exchange boundaries; Python/opaque UDFs, coalesce(N) collapsing upstream stages, and certain streaming micro-batch plans bypass AQE skew splitting.
anti_pattern_traps: assuming AQE automatically fixes all skew regardless of shuffle boundaries or UDFs

prompt: Why does WHERE DATE(event_ts) = '2026-11-01' still trigger a full-table scan and burn budget on a BigQuery TIMESTAMP-partitioned table, and how do you prevent it?
expected_tradeoffs: Wrapping the partition column in a function prevents static/dynamic partition pruning; enforce require_partition_filter=true and rewrite as half-open range predicates event_ts >= ... AND event_ts < ....
anti_pattern_traps: wrapping partition columns in DATE()/CAST() without noting full-scan cost

prompt: Why does a dbt incremental merge model with a 1-day lookback silently drop or corrupt aggregates on late-arriving events, and why does unique_key fail when nullable?
expected_tradeoffs: SQL MERGE evaluates NULL = NULL as UNKNOWN (creating duplicates); fixed 1-day lookback misses p99 late arrivals, whereas partition-level insert_overwrite or microbatch trades compute idempotency for simplicity.
anti_pattern_traps: using SQL MERGE on nullable unique_key without COALESCE/surrogate key or sufficient lookback

prompt: How do concurrent or out-of-order updates corrupt SCD Type 2 effective date ranges, and how do you enforce non-overlapping intervals?
expected_tradeoffs: Naive UPDATE+INSERT races produce overlapping intervals or multiple is_current=true rows; half-open [valid_from, valid_to) intervals with deterministic LEAD() rebuilds or GiST exclusion constraints guarantee disjointness.
anti_pattern_traps: closed [start, end] intervals or non-atomic UPDATE then INSERT without locking/merge

prompt: What happens to a primary PostgreSQL database when a Debezium/pgoutput consumer crashes for 48 hours with an active logical replication slot, and how do you bound the blast radius?
expected_tradeoffs: An inactive slot pins WAL segments indefinitely until pg_wal exhausts disk and crashes Postgres; max_slot_wal_keep_size bounds disk usage at the cost of invalidating the slot and requiring re-snapshot.
anti_pattern_traps: enabling logical replication slots without max_slot_wal_keep_size and WAL lag alerting

prompt: Why does SELECT count(*) FROM events after an upsert still return duplicate rows in ClickHouse ReplacingMergeTree?
expected_tradeoffs: ReplacingMergeTree deduplicates asynchronously only during background part merges; FINAL or argMax/GROUP BY at query time gives exact results at the cost of extra read-time CPU/memory.
anti_pattern_traps: assuming ReplacingMergeTree provides immediate synchronous deduplication on read

prompt: Why does running Delta Lake VACUUM table RETAIN 0 HOURS corrupt concurrent readers and break time-travel?
expected_tradeoffs: Zero-hour retention deletes Parquet files still referenced by active long-running queries or streaming checkpoints; retention must exceed max query/checkpoint duration (default 168h).
anti_pattern_traps: running VACUUM RETAIN 0 HOURS in production without disabling/checking active readers

prompt: Why does a Flink event-time windowed join stall completely when 1 of 32 Kafka partitions has zero traffic?
expected_tradeoffs: Global operator watermark advances as min(partition watermarks), so an idle partition freezes the join window; withIdleness() advances past idle partitions at the risk of late-data drops if traffic resumes.
anti_pattern_traps: ignoring idle partition watermark propagation in multi-partition Kafka sources

prompt: What breaks in Flink when RocksDB state grows large and you enable unaligned checkpoints without sizing managed memory and backpressure buffers?
expected_tradeoffs: Unaligned checkpoints persist in-flight network buffers to unblock barriers under backpressure, inflating checkpoint size and recovery time; RocksDB off-heap memory also causes container cgroup OOMs if overhead is under-reserved.
anti_pattern_traps: enabling unaligned checkpoints blindly without analyzing backpressure root cause

prompt: Why does a 10-second streaming micro-batch sinking to Iceberg/Delta on S3 degrade metadata planning to minutes within days?
expected_tradeoffs: High-frequency commits create thousands of tiny Parquet files and bloated manifest trees; async bin-packing compaction + expire_snapshots restores scan/planning speed while adding background compute cost.
anti_pattern_traps: writing sub-MB micro-batch files directly to lakehouse tables without compaction

prompt: Why does renaming a column or widening INT32 to INT64 in raw Parquet break historical queries, and how do Iceberg/Delta field-ID mappings solve it?
expected_tradeoffs: Plain Parquet resolves columns by name (returning NULLs on rename) and often rejects INT32->INT64 across files; Iceberg/Delta field-ID tracking decouples logical names from physical column IDs.
anti_pattern_traps: renaming columns in-place on raw Hive/Parquet tables without field-ID column mapping

prompt: Why does DuckDB throw a Conflicting lock error in a multi-worker service, and what happens when a hash join exceeds RAM?
expected_tradeoffs: DuckDB enforces a single-writer/multiple-reader file lock per .duckdb database; large joins require explicit memory_limit and temp_directory for disk spill instead of OOMing.
anti_pattern_traps: using a single .duckdb file for concurrent multi-process writes

prompt: Why does Debezium fail or lock a production MySQL/PostgreSQL table during initial snapshot, and how does DBLog watermarking avoid long locks?
expected_tradeoffs: Full-table lock snapshots block production writes; DBLog incremental chunked snapshots interleave watermarked SELECT chunks with binlog events at the cost of slightly longer initial backfill.
anti_pattern_traps: running blocking initial snapshots on large production OLTP tables

prompt: Why does an Airflow/Dagster DAG using INSERT INTO ... WHERE created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 day' duplicate or corrupt data on backfills?
expected_tradeoffs: Using wall-clock NOW() makes retries non-idempotent; scoping writes to logical data_interval_start/end with atomic partition overwrite or MERGE guarantees repeatable backfills.
anti_pattern_traps: using wall-clock NOW()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() in backfillable pipeline filters

prompt: Why does micro-partitioned cloud MPP warehouse pruning degrade after random UPDATE/DELETEs despite initial ORDER BY ingestion, and why does COPY INTO skip a corrected file?
expected_tradeoffs: Random DML splits/overlaps micro-partition min/max ranges until reclustering runs; COPY INTO deduplicates by file checksum/name for 64 days unless FORCE=TRUE or a new filename is used.
anti_pattern_traps: assuming initial load sort order persists permanently under random DML

prompt: Why is DELETE FROM iceberg_table WHERE user_id = '...' insufficient for GDPR Right-to-be-Forgotten compliance?
expected_tradeoffs: Log-structured deletes leave PII physically intact in older snapshots/Parquet files until compaction + expire_snapshots purge them; crypto-shredding per-user keys enables instant logical erasure.
anti_pattern_traps: claiming a single SQL DELETE satisfies GDPR erasure in an append-only lakehouse

prompt: Why does forcing a BROADCAST join hint on a 50 MB Parquet dimension table OOM Spark executors?
expected_tradeoffs: 50 MB Zstd/Snappy Parquet expands 5-10x uncompressed plus JVM object/hash-map overhead, exceeding driver/executor broadcast memory.
anti_pattern_traps: sizing broadcast thresholds from compressed Parquet file size instead of in-memory footprint

prompt: How do naive timestamp strings without timezones or float64 money columns pass schema checks yet silently corrupt analytics?
expected_tradeoffs: Structural type checks miss semantic drift (DST gaps, floating-point pennies); enforce ODCS/Deequ semantic contracts with UTC TIMESTAMPTZ and fixed-point DECIMAL.
anti_pattern_traps: using FLOAT/DOUBLE for monetary amounts or timezone-naive strings for event timestamps

prompt: When does Data Vault 2.0 (Hubs, Links, Satellites + PIT/Bridge) pay off over Kimball dimensional modeling, and why does One Big Table (OBT) break down under multi-grain facts?
expected_tradeoffs: Data Vault excels at multi-source auditability and parallel ingestion but requires PIT/Bridge tables for BI speed; OBT simplifies single-grain BI but causes double-counting fan-out across mixed grains.
anti_pattern_traps: joining different fact grains into OBT without grain alignment or querying raw Data Vault directly from BI

prompt: Why does a naive Bronze -> Silver -> Gold Medallion pipeline leak corrupt data to BI dashboards on partial failures, and how does Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) branching prevent it?
expected_tradeoffs: Direct-to-main writes expose partial/unvalidated batches to readers; WAP writes to an isolated branch, runs quality assertions, and atomically fast-forwards the main branch only on pass.
anti_pattern_traps: mutating production Gold tables before running quality assertions

prompt: How do you enforce cross-domain schema compatibility, PII classification, and global lineage in a Data Mesh without re-creating a central bottleneck?
expected_tradeoffs: Centralized manual review kills domain velocity; automated CI/CD contract checks (ODCS + OpenLineage + automated PII tagging) enforce global invariants while keeping domain autonomy.
anti_pattern_traps: equating Data Mesh with unmanaged domain silos lacking automated contract/lineage enforcement

prompt: Why do independence assumptions in single-column histograms cause a Cost-Based Optimizer (CBO) to pick catastrophic nested-loop or broadcast joins on correlated predicates?
expected_tradeoffs: Single-column histograms multiply selectivities, underestimating row counts by orders of magnitude; multi-column sketches/stats + runtime bloom/AQE re-planning recover at slight planning/runtime overhead.
anti_pattern_traps: relying purely on static single-column histograms for multi-attribute skewed joins

prompt: Under what write/read/range-scan ratios does an LSM-tree's write-amplification advantage over a B-Tree reverse into read-amplification and compaction-stall tail-latency degradation?
expected_tradeoffs: LSM-trees convert random writes into sequential SSTable flushes (low write latency) but pay read amplification across levels/tombstones and compaction I/O spikes under heavy point-lookup or range-delete workloads.
anti_pattern_traps: assuming LSM-trees strictly dominate B-Trees on read-heavy or tombstone-heavy range workloads
